generated_output.summary: The `/fast` command acts purely as a toggle instead of accepting explicit state modifiers like `/fast off` or `/fast on`, which causes users to inadvertently remain in fast mode and exhaust rate limits.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The CLI command parsing logic for `/fast` interprets the input solely as a binary switch flag without parsing sub-arguments (such as `off` or `on`) to set an absolute target state.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Fast Command Parsing Logic
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect symbol handling for the `/fast` command in codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs to verify how arguments are currently ignored and the state is toggled.

step_by_step_plan.title: Parse Optional Arguments for State Modifiers
step_by_step_plan.description: Update the command parser in codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs to accept optional 'on' or 'off' arguments following the `/fast` command.

step_by_step_plan.title: Implement Absolute State Setting
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the execution branch to set the fast mode state explicitly based on the parsed argument ('on' -> true, 'off' -> false) while preserving bare toggle behavior when no argument is supplied.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Regression Tests for Explicit Fast State Modifiers
step_by_step_plan.description: Add unit and integration tests verifying that `/fast on`, `/fast off`, and bare `/fast` correctly set the expected fast mode state.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The process of reading text input after a command slash and extracting parameters or sub-commands.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Developers need precise control over CLI options so they can specify exact states rather than guessing toggle states.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Fixing the issue requires parsing optional arguments like 'on' or 'off' following the `/fast` command rather than treating it as a bare toggle.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Toggles flip the current state blindly, whereas idempotent setters ensure the system reaches a specific known state regardless of prior state.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Idempotency prevents user error and resource waste caused by mismatched assumptions about current system state.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Users expect `/fast off` to be an idempotent setter that guarantees fast mode is disabled, preventing accidental rate-limit exhaustion.

common_pitfalls: Changing other slash commands unintentionally while refactoring command parsing.
Forgetting to handle case-insensitivity for 'on' and 'off' arguments (e.g., 'OFF', 'Off', 'off').
